text:
Hm, they said this model was better at writing, but it still sounds pretty obviously like an LLM-written script.

Short punchy sentences. Strung together one after the other like lights on a Christmas tree. Could sound repetitive. Or maybe just lacking in variance. And then it hits you. "This is an AI script." That's why it sounds like a junior at an advertising firm. No nuance. No flow. Just a string of statements. And here's the kicker. That's actually a legitimate writing style — one that's actually used by professionals. Just not everywhere. Not through an entire several-minute presentation, for instance.

text: I use AI in my work every day. I come from a marketing background and also do some creative work. Nowadays, with the new AI tools coming out, such as Anthropic's Fable 5.1 and GPT-6, there's a lot to explore. No doubt, these are very good, but when I see their price, I think more about whether it will be worth using them rather than being excited. Still, something like the Deep Seek Flash or glm 5.3 flash I am still using these because their output is good. I compared them with Fable 5 and GPT-6, but they are workable. Plus, their price is quite affordable. I often think about whether these new tools will provide real-life benefits unless there is a heavily funded project or a highly budget project involved. AllEssential does not become affordable for a real user until I don't think it can be mastered. Yes, some creators or companies can use it in limited ways, but in daily life, the majority are not able to make any changes.
